result:
If I could change the world in one way, I'd make it so that people felt genuine pain when they lied to themselves.

Not social consequences. Not external punishment. An internal, automatic discomfort—like a headache or nausea—whenever they chose a comforting story over what the evidence actually suggests. It wouldn't stop bad behavior entirely, but it would make self-deception expensive. A lot of the world's most persistent problems (tribalism, policy disasters, personal ruin) run on the fuel of people preferring to be wrong in ways that feel good rather than right in ways that don't.

Everything else—technology, institutions, even intelligence—seems secondary to that one fracture.
